// MeshStandardMaterial reduced to Blinn-Phong: the scenes use one
// point light + roughness/metalness, so a full PBR BRDF would buy
// nothing measurable — the approximation is the standard one:
//
//   diffuse  = color · (N·L)⁺            — Lambert term.
//   specular = light · (N·H)⁺^shininess  — Blinn half-vector term.
//   shininess = (1−roughness)·128 + 2    — maps roughness to exponent:
//             roughness 1 → ~2 (broad, matte), 0 → ~130 (tight glint).
//   metalness scales the specular tint toward the base color (metals
//   reflect colored light; dielectrics reflect white).
//
// Ambient is a flat 8% floor — enough to keep unlit faces readable in
// the dark-space scenes without a second light source or IBL probe.
//
// Uniform layout: identical to shader_basic.wgsl (see that file's doc
// for the byte map). light_* fields are populated here for real.

struct Frame {
    view_proj : mat4x4<f32>,
    cam_pos   : vec3<f32>,
    time      : f32,
    _pad0     : vec4<f32>,
    light_pos : vec3<f32>,
    _pad1     : f32,
    light_rgb : vec3<f32>,
    _pad2     : f32,
    light_int : f32,
    _pad3     : vec3<f32>,
    canvas    : vec4<f32>,
    model     : mat4x4<f32>,
    mat_color : vec4<f32>,
    mat_emit  : vec4<f32>,
    mat_params: vec4<f32>,   // [0]=unused, [1]=roughness, [2]=metalness
    mat_flags : vec4<f32>,
};

@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> frame : Frame;
@group(1) @binding(0) var tex : texture_2d<f32>;
@group(1) @binding(1) var smp : sampler;

struct VertexIn {
    @location(0) pos : vec3<f32>,
    @location(1) nrm : vec3<f32>,
    @location(2) uv  : vec2<f32>,
};

struct VertexOut {
    @builtin(position) clip  : vec4<f32>,
    @location(0) uv          : vec2<f32>,
    @location(1) nrm         : vec3<f32>,
    @location(2) world       : vec3<f32>,
};

/// `vs_main` — same matrix chain as basic plus a world-pos varying:
/// the fragment stage needs it for the light vector L.
@vertex
fn vs_main(v : VertexIn) -> VertexOut {
    var out : VertexOut;

    let world = frame.model * vec4<f32>(v.pos, 1.0);

    out.clip  = frame.view_proj * world;
    out.uv    = v.uv;
    out.nrm   = normalize((frame.model * vec4<f32>(v.nrm, 0.0)).xyz);
    out.world = world.xyz;

    return out;
}

/// `fs_main` — Blinn-Phong with the flat ambient floor. All vector
/// math is normalized first (interpolation denormalizes normals —
/// the classic per-fragment shading bug when skipped).
@fragment
fn fs_main(v : VertexOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
    let texel   = textureSample(tex, smp, v.uv);
    let base    = texel * frame.mat_color;
    let n       = normalize(v.nrm);
    let l       = normalize(frame.light_pos - v.world);
    let viewdir = normalize(frame.cam_pos - v.world);
    let h       = normalize(l + viewdir);

    let diff = max(dot(n, l), 0.0);
    let shin = (1.0 - frame.mat_params.y) * 128.0 + 2.0;
    let spec = pow(max(dot(n, h), 0.0), shin);

    // Metalness lerps specular tint: white (dielectric) → base (metal).
    let spec_tint = mix(vec3<f32>(1.0), base.rgb, frame.mat_params.z);

    let lit = base.rgb * (0.08 + diff * frame.light_int * frame.light_rgb)
            + spec_tint * spec * frame.light_int;

    return vec4<f32>(lit + frame.mat_emit.rgb, base.a);
}
// shader_sprite.wgsl — camera-facing billboard (three.js Sprite).
//
// A sprite is a quad that always faces the camera — the classic
// implementation expands the quad in VIEW space, which is exactly
// what this shader does:
//
//   center_view = view · model · vec4(0,0,0,1)   — the sprite's world
//                 position viewed from the eye.
//   view_pos    = center_view + vec4(corner.xy · size, 0, 0)
//               — push each corner outward in VIEW space: the quad
//               can never rotate because view-space x/y is the screen
//               plane by definition.
//   clip        = proj · view_pos
//
// `size` comes from the model matrix's scale (three.js Sprite
// semantics — scale.x/y are the sprite's world-space width/height).
// We extract it as the column lengths of model's upper 3×3, which is
// exact for uniform scale and a documented approximation otherwise.
//
// `view` is the inverse of the camera transform — but the uniform
// carries only view_proj. We recover the view matrix's translation-
// removed rotation by noting the sprite center in view space is
// `view·world_pos`; rather than store a second matrix, we compute
// center_view = view_proj·world and unproject? NO — simpler: view_pos
// needs view-space coordinates, and view = proj⁻¹·view_proj. Since
// the renderer also stores cam_pos, the sprite shader uses the
// standard trick instead: world-space billboard using the camera
// right/up vectors, extracted from view_proj inverse is overkill —
// the view basis is orthonormal, so:
//
//   right_view = (1,0,0), up_view = (0,1,0) — view-space billboarding
//   needs NO basis vectors at all. We still need `view` itself to get
//   the center into view space, and view = inverse(proj)·view_proj
//   only if proj is invertible — it is for finite far planes, but
//   inverse() in WGSL is hand-rolled and 16 divisions per vertex is
//   the wrong cost.
//
// The chosen formulation: the renderer writes view_proj AND we
// bill-board in CLIP space instead — the standard clip-space trick:
//
//   clip = view_proj · world_center, then
//   clip.xy += corner.xy · size_view · clip.w
//
//   ·clip.w keeps the expansion proportional to distance (perspective
//   — a far sprite shrinks exactly like a near one at equal world
//   size). size_view = world_size / (2·tan(fov/2)·dist)·… — instead of
//   that chain we pass the world-space half-size and divide by view
//   depth: corner·size·(clip.w/dist) — and clip.w IS -view_z for a
//   perspective matrix, so:
//
//   clip.xy += corner.xy · size_world · proj_scale
//   where proj_scale = proj[0][0], proj[1][1] extracted from
//   view_proj is not separable (proj·view mixes them) — BUT view has
//   orthonormal columns, so the [0][0] and [1][1] scale survives: NO,
//   it doesn't.
//
// FINAL DESIGN (the honest one): the camera block carries cam_pos —
// the sprite builds its own view basis from (cam_pos → sprite_center):
//   fwd   = normalize(cam_pos − center)
//   right = normalize(cross(world_up, fwd))
//   up    = cross(fwd, right)
//   world_pos = center + (right·corner.x + up·corner.y) · size
// This is the CPU-three.js formulation moved to the vertex shader —
// one cross-product basis per corner (4×/sprite, trivial), exact for
// any projection, no matrix inversion, no clip-space fudge factor.
// Degenerate case (fwd ∥ world_up): cross product → 0 — the fallback
// substitutes (0,0,1) as the up hint, the standard gimbal guard.

struct Frame {
    view_proj : mat4x4<f32>,
    cam_pos   : vec3<f32>,
    time      : f32,
    _pad0     : vec4<f32>,
    light_pos : vec3<f32>,
    _pad1     : f32,
    light_rgb : vec3<f32>,
    _pad2     : f32,
    light_int : f32,
    _pad3     : vec3<f32>,
    canvas    : vec4<f32>,
    model     : mat4x4<f32>,
    mat_color : vec4<f32>,
    mat_emit  : vec4<f32>,
    mat_params: vec4<f32>,
    mat_flags : vec4<f32>,
};

@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> frame : Frame;
@group(1) @binding(0) var tex : texture_2d<f32>;
@group(1) @binding(1) var smp : sampler;

struct VertexIn {
    @location(0) pos : vec3<f32>,   // unit-quad corner (−0.5..0.5)
    @location(1) nrm : vec3<f32>,   // unused — sprites are unlit
    @location(2) uv  : vec2<f32>,
};

struct VertexOut {
    @builtin(position) clip : vec4<f32>,
    @location(0) uv         : vec2<f32>,
};

/// `vs_main` — world-space billboard via a rebuilt camera basis (see
/// the module doc for why this beats clip-space tricks). The model
/// matrix's translation is the sprite center; its column lengths are
//  the world-space quad size (half-extents: the quad spans ±0.5).
@vertex
fn vs_main(v : VertexIn) -> VertexOut {
    var out : VertexOut;

    let center = frame.model[3].xyz;

    // Model scale → world-space quad size. Column lengths of the
    // upper 3×3: |m[:,0]| = scale.x, |m[:,1]| = scale.y.
    let sx = length(frame.model[0].xyz);
    let sy = length(frame.model[1].xyz);

    let fwd = normalize(frame.cam_pos - center);
    var up_hint = vec3<f32>(0.0, 1.0, 0.0);

    // Gimbal guard: fwd ∥ up_hint → cross → 0 → rebase on z.
    if (abs(dot(fwd, up_hint)) > 0.99) {
        up_hint = vec3<f32>(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    }

    let right = normalize(cross(up_hint, fwd));
    let up    = cross(fwd, right);

    let world = center + (right * v.pos.x * sx) + (up * v.pos.y * sy);

    out.clip = frame.view_proj * vec4<f32>(world, 1.0);
    out.uv   = v.uv;

    return out;
}

/// `fs_main` — sprite composite: texel·color + emissive, same as
/// basic (sprites are unlit quads — glows, labels, flares).
@fragment
fn fs_main(v : VertexOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
    let texel = textureSample(tex, smp, v.uv);

    return texel * frame.mat_color + frame.mat_emit;
}
// shader_points.wgsl — point-sprite pipeline (three.js PointsMaterial).
//
// WebGPU has no gl_PointSize — point primitives rasterize as 1px.
// The renderer instead expands every point into a 4-vertex billboard
// quad at upload time (`expand_points` in renderer.rs): the vertex
// stream's `pos` slot carries the shared point CENTER and `uv`
// carries the quad CORNER (−1..1).
//
// Expansion happens in view space like the sprite shader, but cheaper:
// the point is a camera-facing screen-aligned quad, so we can add the
// corner offset AFTER view_proj by using the camera basis trick only
// once — actually simpler still: we build the same world-basis the
// sprite shader uses, since per-vertex cost is tiny (4 verts/point,
// no fragment overdraw beyond the quad).
//
// Point size contract (mat_params.x): world-space half-size — the
// quad's world radius. dpr compensation (canvas.w/dpr fields) is for
// CSS-specified sizes; world-space sizes scale correctly through the
// projection automatically — no dpr term needed.
//
// Circular falloff: the fragment stage discards fragments outside the
// unit circle (corner length > 1) — square points look wrong in space
// scenes — and applies a soft edge (smoothstep) for anti-aliasing
// without MSAA-dependent alpha-to-coverage.

struct Frame {
    view_proj : mat4x4<f32>,
    cam_pos   : vec3<f32>,
    time      : f32,
    _pad0     : vec4<f32>,
    light_pos : vec3<f32>,
    _pad1     : f32,
    light_rgb : vec3<f32>,
    _pad2     : f32,
    light_int : f32,
    _pad3     : vec3<f32>,
    canvas    : vec4<f32>,
    model     : mat4x4<f32>,
    mat_color : vec4<f32>,
    mat_emit  : vec4<f32>,
    mat_params: vec4<f32>,   // [0] = world-space half-size
    mat_flags : vec4<f32>,
};

@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> frame : Frame;
@group(1) @binding(0) var tex : texture_2d<f32>;
@group(1) @binding(1) var smp : sampler;

struct VertexIn {
    @location(0) pos    : vec3<f32>,   // point CENTER (shared by 4 verts)
    @location(1) nrm    : vec3<f32>,   // unused — points are unlit
    @location(2) corner : vec2<f32>,   // quad corner (−1..1), packed in uv
};

struct VertexOut {
    @builtin(position) clip   : vec4<f32>,
    @location(0) corner       : vec2<f32>,
};

/// `vs_main` — billboard expansion via the same rebuilt-basis trick
/// as the sprite shader (see shader_sprite.wgsl's doc): center →
/// world → basis-offset by corner·half_size → project.
@vertex
fn vs_main(v : VertexIn) -> VertexOut {
    var out : VertexOut;

    let center = (frame.model * vec4<f32>(v.pos, 1.0)).xyz;
    let size   = frame.mat_params.x;
    let fwd    = normalize(frame.cam_pos - center);
    var up_hint = vec3<f32>(0.0, 1.0, 0.0);

    if (abs(dot(fwd, up_hint)) > 0.99) {
        up_hint = vec3<f32>(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    }

    let right = normalize(cross(up_hint, fwd));
    let up    = cross(fwd, right);
    let world = center + (right * v.corner.x + up * v.corner.y) * size;

    out.clip   = frame.view_proj * vec4<f32>(world, 1.0);
    out.corner = v.corner;

    return out;
}

/// `fs_main` — circular point sprite: discard outside the unit
/// circle, smoothstep edge AA, texel·color + emissive composite.
/// The discard is a real `discard` (not alpha 0) — additive point
/// clouds must not write transparent depth.
@fragment
fn fs_main(v : VertexOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
    // Sample BEFORE the discard — implicit-derivative calls must sit
    // in unconditionally-uniform control flow; a post-discard call is
    // legal on most validators but demote-after-sample ordering is
    // universally safe and identical in output (the discarded
    // fragment never presents).
    let r = length(v.corner);
    let texel = textureSample(tex, smp, v.corner * 0.5 + vec2<f32>(0.5));

    if (r > 1.0) {
        discard;
    }

    // Edge AA: alpha ramps 1→0 over the outer 20% of the radius —
    // wide enough to hide the quad edge at point sizes ≥4px, narrow
    // enough that small points stay solid.
    let alpha = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.8, 1.0, r);

    return (texel * frame.mat_color + frame.mat_emit) * alpha;
}
// shader_instanced.wgsl — instanced mesh pipeline (three.js
// InstancedMesh with MeshBasicMaterial — the star-field use case:
// thousands of identical star quads with per-instance transforms).
//
// Vertex buffer slot 1 carries a per-instance mat4x4 as four
// step=instance float32x4 attributes at locations 3-6 (the web-sys
// pipeline builder in renderer.rs declares them as four vec4 params —
// WGSL validates a mat4x4 vertex input inconsistently across drivers,
// so the mat is rebuilt in-shader from its column vecs).
//
// Transform order (three.js semantics):
//   world = model · instance · pos
// `model` is the InstancedMesh node's own transform (usually identity
// — instances are already world-space in star-field), `instance` is
// the per-instance TRS written by scene.set_instance().
//
// Fragment: same unlit composite as shader_basic — instanced glows
// are additive-blended, which the pipeline key already encodes.

struct Frame {
    view_proj : mat4x4<f32>,
    cam_pos   : vec3<f32>,
    time      : f32,
    _pad0     : vec4<f32>,
    light_pos : vec3<f32>,
    _pad1     : f32,
    light_rgb : vec3<f32>,
    _pad2     : f32,
    light_int : f32,
    _pad3     : vec3<f32>,
    canvas    : vec4<f32>,
    model     : mat4x4<f32>,
    mat_color : vec4<f32>,
    mat_emit  : vec4<f32>,
    mat_params: vec4<f32>,
    mat_flags : vec4<f32>,
};

@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> frame : Frame;
@group(1) @binding(0) var tex : texture_2d<f32>;
@group(1) @binding(1) var smp : sampler;

struct VertexIn {
    @location(0) pos : vec3<f32>,
    @location(1) nrm : vec3<f32>,
    @location(2) uv  : vec2<f32>,
    // Instance matrix columns — location 3-6, step=instance.
    @location(3) i0 : vec4<f32>,
    @location(4) i1 : vec4<f32>,
    @location(5) i2 : vec4<f32>,
    @location(6) i3 : vec4<f32>,
};

struct VertexOut {
    @builtin(position) clip : vec4<f32>,
    @location(0) uv         : vec2<f32>,
};

/// `vs_main` — rebuild the instance matrix from its four column
/// attributes and apply the standard chain: model·instance·pos →
/// view_proj. Mat4 storage is column-major (math.rs's .m layout —
/// m[0..4] is column 0), matching WGSL's mat4x4 constructor order.
@vertex
fn vs_main(v : VertexIn) -> VertexOut {
    var out : VertexOut;

    let inst = mat4x4<f32>(v.i0, v.i1, v.i2, v.i3);
    let world = frame.model * inst * vec4<f32>(v.pos, 1.0);

    out.clip = frame.view_proj * world;
    out.uv   = v.uv;

    return out;
}

/// `fs_main` — unlit texel·color + emissive, identical to basic:
/// instancing is a vertex-stage concern only.
@fragment
fn fs_main(v : VertexOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
    let texel = textureSample(tex, smp, v.uv);

    return texel * frame.mat_color + frame.mat_emit;
}
// shader_basic.wgsl — unlit mesh pipeline (three.js MeshBasicMaterial).
//
// Vertex: pos → model → view_proj, passing normal/uv/world-pos through
// for the fragment stage. Fragment: mat_color · texture + emissive —
// no lighting terms, matching MeshBasicMaterial semantics (sky domes,
// glow shells, flat-colored geometry).
//
// # Uniform block layout (mirrors renderer.rs FRAME_F32S, byte-exact)
//
//   f32 0-15   view_proj  — proj·view, multiplies on the left.
//   f32 16-18  cam_pos    — world-space eye (unused here; kept so the
//              block is ONE layout across all 5 shaders — a single
//              bind group serves every pipeline).
//   f32 19     time       — seconds since mount (shader clocks).
//   f32 20-23  _pad
//   f32 24-26  light_pos  — the scene point light (unused in basic).
//   f32 27     _pad
//   f32 28-30  light_rgb  — light color (unused in basic).
//   f32 31     _pad
//   f32 32     light_int  — intensity (unused in basic).
//   f32 36-39  canvas     — (w, h, 1/h, dpr) in device px.
//   f32 48-63  model      — the node's world matrix.
//   f32 64-67  mat_color  — material base color rgba.
//   f32 68-71  mat_emit   — emissive additive tint.
//   f32 72-75  mat_params — kind-specific (unused in basic).
//   f32 76-79  mat_flags  — (tex_id, side, blending, transparent).
//
// The struct is declared identically in every scene3d shader — the
// shared `@group(0)` bind group is interchangeable across pipelines
// only when layouts match field-for-field.

struct Frame {
    view_proj : mat4x4<f32>,
    cam_pos   : vec3<f32>,
    time      : f32,
    _pad0     : vec4<f32>,
    light_pos : vec3<f32>,
    _pad1     : f32,
    light_rgb : vec3<f32>,
    _pad2     : f32,
    light_int : f32,
    _pad3     : vec3<f32>,
    canvas    : vec4<f32>,
    model     : mat4x4<f32>,
    mat_color : vec4<f32>,
    mat_emit  : vec4<f32>,
    mat_params: vec4<f32>,
    mat_flags : vec4<f32>,
};

@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> frame : Frame;
@group(1) @binding(0) var tex : texture_2d<f32>;
@group(1) @binding(1) var smp : sampler;

/// `VertexIn` — the 32B interleaved stream from renderer.rs:
/// position(0) | normal(1) | uv(2).
struct VertexIn {
    @location(0) pos : vec3<f32>,
    @location(1) nrm : vec3<f32>,
    @location(2) uv  : vec2<f32>,
};

/// `VertexOut` — the varying payload the rasterizer interpolates:
/// clip position plus the fragment inputs.
struct VertexOut {
    @builtin(position) clip : vec4<f32>,
    @location(0) uv         : vec2<f32>,
    @location(1) nrm        : vec3<f32>,
};

/// `vs_main` — one matrix chain: world = model·pos, clip =
/// view_proj·world. The normal transforms by model's upper 3×3 (valid
//  for the uniform/rigid scales these scenes use — non-uniform scale
//  would need the inverse-transpose; star-field/earth scales are
//  uniform, documented in scene.rs).
@vertex
fn vs_main(v : VertexIn) -> VertexOut {
    var out : VertexOut;

    let world = frame.model * vec4<f32>(v.pos, 1.0);

    out.clip = frame.view_proj * world;
    out.uv   = v.uv;
    out.nrm  = normalize((frame.model * vec4<f32>(v.nrm, 0.0)).xyz);

    return out;
}

/// `fs_main` — unlit composite: texel · color + emissive. Untextured
/// materials bind the 1×1 white texel so the multiply is unconditional
/// (no pipeline fork by texture presence — the registry guarantees a
/// valid view at slot 0 for every material).
@fragment
fn fs_main(v : VertexOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
    let texel = textureSample(tex, smp, v.uv);

    return texel * frame.mat_color + frame.mat_emit;
}
